title: Book
intro: Book moves from minimising a mistake to fearing the loss of a coherent self. The speaker cannot put bad memories aside, yet fears forgetting who he is; neither remembering nor forgetting feels fully under his control. Advice to care less is qualified as something to try, not an achieved immunity. The final book offers a modest form of persistence. He keeps reading the life he is in, without claiming to have authored every event or solved its meaning.
reading: Failed minimisation leads inward; unwanted memory coexists with fear of self-loss; reading offers ongoing effort rather than mastery.

revisions.37-phrase-too-far: The opening treats a serious consequence as an overextended game and answers it with 'next time'. But the ensuing memories will not respect that casual closure. The movement makes the understatement revealing: the speaker is trying to limit the event's importance before describing how much mental space it occupies. Nothing in the lyric identifies the event, so filling in a particular scandal would replace this observed pattern with invention.
revisions.37-phrase-belief: The vocabulary narrows from lacking a larger faith, to doubting himself, to losing confidence. The threat then shifts from other people to his own ability to recognise himself. This progression gives the verse more shape than a general list of dark feelings. It describes the disappearance of successive places where certainty might have rested, without requiring a clinical explanation for the inner argument.
revisions.editorial-37-forget-self: Bad memories keep returning, yet forgetting is also what he fears. The conflict is not simply wanting a blank mind: he wants relief from some parts of experience without losing the self those experiences have helped form. The unfamiliar road and lifelong solitude make that task feel unsupported. The line is most powerful when the two risks remain together, rather than treating memory as wholly harmful or wholly protective.
revisions.editorial-37-life-book: He becomes a reader, not an all-powerful author or somebody who has finished the lesson. The repeated continuing action answers the earlier wish to dismiss the mistake and move on: understanding will take more time than that. The book does not promise that every painful event has a useful meaning. It offers the smaller commitment to remain engaged with a life whose meaning is still being worked out.
